text:
Tye Kartye went undrafted, worked his way through the AHL, and arrived on Broadway as a fourth-line energy forward. Twenty-two games into his first full Rangers season he is something else: 16:49 a night (up from 11:58), a slice of the power play, and 14 points.

The production is backed by the process. His own chances are up to 1.02 expected goals per 60 from 0.46 (expected goals measure the quality of the looks), and his seven goals are close to his 6.3 expected. The Rangers have also scored 4.5 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, so if anything his assist total is light. At 5v5 New York gets 58.6% of the expected goals when he plays.

EDGE backs up the eye test, too: his top shot speed ranks in the 87th percentile and his skating distance in the 86th, and he has 57 hits. Sports Illustrated is already calling him a building block. Our numbers see a breakout with real legs under it, not a hot month.
